observed_problem: The production-control workflow validates the worktree against the Production State pinned implementation commit but executes survey_handoff_v2/survey_orchestrator_v2 from a separate control-src checkout of current main. A later main-side Core change can therefore change executable behavior without changing the State-pinned implementation identity being verified.
expected_behavior: Every production action must execute the exact implementation-control bytes whose commit identity is pinned in Production State. The workflow driver itself must also fail if the currently dispatched workflow definition differs from the worktree/pinned workflow definition.
actual_behavior: PYTHONPATH and script paths point to control-src while verify_runtime_implementation inspects worktree. This splits executable identity from the repository tree whose implementation provenance is attested.
production_workaround: External W33/SP001 production remains blocked until the coherent Core v2 candidate is Human-reviewed and merged; control/release now execute State-pinned worktree code and verify active workflow identity.
improvement_action: Execute all Core v2 Python entrypoints from the production worktree, install dependencies from that worktree, require the currently dispatched main workflow file to be byte-identical to the worktree workflow file, and retain verify_runtime_implementation as the pinned-commit control-root check.
